newsitem.title: LEBANON: Syria says Beirut opposition extends hand to Israel.
newsitem.headline: Syria says Beirut opposition extends hand to Israel.

text.p: Syrian Vice-President Abdel Halim Khaddam in an interview published on Tuesday accused some Lebanese opposition leaders of extending their hands to Israel and working to destabilise their own country.

"As for the non-parliamentary opposition, its leaders take stands against the country. How can we support an opposition against the country's security and stability; an opposition that extends its hand to Israel?" Khaddam told the Beirut daily newspaper as-Safir in an interview.

Khaddam did not name the leaders but three prominent Lebanese Christian figures fiercely opposed to Syria's dominant role in Lebanon last month announced the formation of an opposition front against the Syrian-backed Beirut government.

The "National Gathering" front whose birth was announced in Beirut on November 21 groups the supporters of rebel General Michel Aoun and former president Amin Gemayel -- who both live in Paris -- and Dori Chamoun, the Beirut-based head of the National Liberal Party.

The three leaders vowed to work to regain what they called Lebanon's lost sovereignty. Damascus is Beirut's main power broker with 35,000 troops stationed over two thirds of Lebanon. Israel occupies a border zone in south Lebanon.
Asked about recent anti-Syrian attacks inside Lebanon, Khaddam hinted that some of them were sponsored by Israel.
The attacks included a December 19 incident in which Syrian workers in a bus were machinegunned in a mainly Christian area north of Beirut, killing the driver and wounding some passengers.

Khaddam dismissed criticisms levelled against the Lebanese government by some Christian opposition leaders including Aoun and Chamoun after a wave of arrests of Christians following the attacks. Most of those arrested have been released.
"When some individuals linked to Israel undertake actions against state security and the government then takes measures, it is said that a certain sect is being targeted. This is not true," he added.
